name: PyVista
role: Pythonic VTK wrapper that renders meshes off-screen to PNG with numpy image access
summary: Python library over VTK for meshes, point clouds and volumes. Plotter(off_screen=True) renders a fixed camera and window size to a PNG or a numpy array with no window, and can write movies. Choose it over vedo when you want the larger API and numpy image return; both sit on VTK.
use_when: Render a mesh or point cloud to a PNG or numpy array from Python with a fixed camera
Script scientific visualisation stills where the VTK route is already chosen
Read the rendered pixels back as an array for checks or compositing
avoid_when: Build a complete animated production scene: Blender
Do lightweight triangle-mesh processing only: Trimesh
Render an interactive browser-based VTK scene: vtk.js

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install pyvista==0.49.3

notes: 2026-11-27: the lead named uv pip install pyvista; a plain pip venv worked. Python >=3.10 required.
2026-11-27: off-screen rendering worked headless on macOS arm64 with no Xvfb, from an agent shell.

assessment.rationale: PyPI 0.49.3 uploaded 2026-11-24, MIT per installed metadata, VTK BSD. Versus vedo, whose fixture only round-trips VTP, PyVista has a proven headless macOS render and returns pixels as a numpy array. It overlaps vedo, so keep it as the render-checked VTK route and vedo as the alternative; vtk-js is browser-only and open3d is a different stack.

evidence.result: Off-screen Plotter rendered an orange sphere to 960x540 PNG headless; two processes gave identical pixels, SHA-256 ca5bdeb8...d61a; sphere 524 px, centred, corners equal background. Two bounds failed first run and were replaced.
evidence.scope: One lit sphere, fixed camera, SSAA, macOS arm64 headless; not other platforms, drivers, movies or textures. Two checks were redefined after a first-run failure.
